verdict.rationale: Mastra is an open-source TypeScript framework that is explicitly self-hostable at no cost. It deploys to any Node.js-compatible environment, runs on Node, Bun, Deno or Cloudflare, and includes a local Studio, so agents can run on your own infrastructure without the vendor's hosted platform. A community comment about license wording concerns third-party hosted resale, not self-hosting, and does not contradict this. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of fully self-hosted production deployments, and documentation that storage and observability backends can run on self-managed infrastructure without vendor services.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run my agents entirely on my own infrastructure with no dependence on the vendor's platform

citations.quote: Self host your Mastra projects ... Free Apache 2.0 licensed $0/ month ... Build and host agents anywhere
Mastra applications can be deployed to any Node.js-compatible environment. You can deploy a Mastra server or integrate with an existing web framework.
Mastra can run against any of these runtime environments: - Node.js `v22.13.0` or later - Bun - Deno - Cloudflare
Open Studio at [`http://localhost:4111`](http://localhost:4111) to test your agent and inspect its runs.
